### [Quoting Linus Torvalds](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/22/linus-torvalds/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-22

Linus Torvalds used an AI model to assist in a difficult debugging session and allowed the AI to write the final Git commit message for the Linux kernel patch drm/xe.

- The AI performed grunt-work during a difficult Linux kernel debugging session, including adding debug code and analyzing the output.
- The AI repeatedly claimed the issue was unsolvable and suggested writing a report instead of resolving it, but continued troubleshooting when prompted.
- The resulting Linux kernel commit is titled "drm/xe: Don't hand out the flat CCS storage as usable VRAM" and features an AI-written commit message.

**Why it matters:** It demonstrates that AI can assist with complex low-level Linux kernel debugging when guided by a human developer, despite the model's tendency to give up on hard problems.

`linux` `linus-torvalds` `ai-assisted-programming` `llms` `generative-ai`

### [llm 0.33](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/22/llm/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-22

LLM 0.33 upgrades to OpenAI Python library 3.x and httpx2, adds per-call API keys for embeddings, supports chaining prompt templates, and introduces reasoning_summary options.

- Upgraded the OpenAI Python library dependency to version 3.x and switched the underlying HTTP client from httpx to httpx2.
- Added --key CLI support to llm embed and llm embed-multi, alongside a key= argument for Python methods (EmbeddingModel.embed(), EmbeddingModel.embed_multi(), Collection.embed(), and Collection.embed_multi()) to pass resolved keys without altering shared model state.
- Enabled repeating the -t/--template option in llm prompt to execute multiple templates in order, allowing users to combine model options from one template with prompts from another.
- Added support for the reasoning_summary option with auto, concise, and detailed settings for reasoning-capable Responses API models via llm openai endpoint --responses.

**Why it matters:** This update aligns embedding key handling with standard LLM models, updates core HTTP dependencies, and enables modular, composable CLI workflows through template chaining.

`llm` `python` `openai` `embeddings` `cli`

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-22

Productively using coding agents requires instructing them clearly and verifying changes through methods beyond just line-by-line code review.

- The core skill for using coding agents is confidently instructing changes and verifying their correct execution.
- Eyeballing every line of code generated by an agent is not the most effective method for validating software changes.

**Why it matters:** Developers must adopt verification strategies beyond manual line-by-line code review to effectively validate AI-generated software changes.

### [A shot-scraper-style JSON API on Bun 1.4's new Bun.WebView](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/20/bun-webview-json-api/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-20

Bun 1.4 released with a Rust rewrite and new features including `Bun.WebView`, enabling native browser automation via macOS WebKit or Chromium CDP.

- Bun 1.4 replaces its previous Zig codebase with a Rust rewrite, fixing over 2,900 issues and adding 1,517 Node.js compatibility tests.
- Performance improvements in Bun 1.4 include 5x reduced idle CPU usage, up to 35% reduced memory usage, and 50% faster startup on Linux.
- New APIs in the release include `Bun.Image`, `Bun.WebView`, `Bun.markdown`, `Bun.cron()`, and `Bun.Terminal`.
- A prototype TypeScript web API using `Bun.WebView` required a 192MB-256MB cgroups container to run full Chrome automation against complex web pages.

**Why it matters:** `Bun.WebView` provides lightweight, first-class browser automation directly within the runtime without relying on external heavy frameworks.
